exposure: First-week gut microbiota composition (alpha diversity, community structures/clusters)
outcome: Hospital admissions for viral lower respiratory tract infections (vLRTIs) in the first 2 years of life
cohort: The study included 1082 babies from the Baby Biome Study (BBS) in the UK, born between Jan 1, 2016, and Dec 31, 2017, who had a sequenced first-week stool sample and successful data linkage.
finding: Higher first-week gut microbiota alpha diversity was associated with reduced rates of vLRTI hospital admission, and specific microbiota clusters (mixed or Bifidobacterium breve dominated) were independently associated with increased vLRTI admission rates compared to a Bifidobacterium longum dominated cluster.
mod_finding: Three microbiota clusters were identified, with cluster 3 (Bifidobacterium longum dominated) found only in vaginally born babies, while clusters 1 and 2 were observed in babies born both vaginally and by caesarean section.
gest_age: Most babies were born at term (92% >=37 weeks gestational age and 99% >35 weeks gestational age).
